lightningGuard.pin.description: Which Raspberry Pi GPIO line drives the lightning relay (the GPIO plugin's lightningOut). The browser asks for the relay through the same connection as the other indicator lines (directly or through Cloud Relay); switch the relay on under Settings → Alerts → Lightning guard. In Cloud Relay mode set these on the Rig Bridge setup page instead.
lightningGuard.pin.failSafe: Fail-safe: energise the relay to keep the antenna connected
lightningGuard.pin.failSafeHint: With fail-safe on, power loss, a crash or a stopped Rig Bridge releases the relay and the antenna is disconnected. Wire the antenna through the contacts that close when the coil is energised (NO).
lightningGuard.pin.gpioOff: The GPIO plugin is not running — enable "Raspberry Pi GPIO" on the Rig Bridge setup page (Plugins).
lightningGuard.pin.gpioRunning: GPIO plugin running ({{backend}}) · lightning relay: {{relay}} · displays reporting: {{displays}}
lightningGuard.pin.headless: Also run the guard inside Rig Bridge (protects with no browser open)
lightningGuard.pin.headlessHint: Rig Bridge then watches Blitzortung itself. Your station's location and the radii, all-clear time, hysteresis, repeat-alert and relay settings from Settings → Alerts → Lightning guard reach it with the indicators this display sends and are kept by the bridge — no need to push again after changing them. It counts as one more display: the relay is engaged while it or any open display wants it.
lightningGuard.pin.hold: Hold the relay for the all-clear time when a display goes quiet
lightningGuard.pin.needsBridge: Enable Rig Bridge above to assign the relay line.
lightningGuard.pin.pinHint: empty = off · suggested 25 (header pin 22) · "P22" also works
lightningGuard.pin.title: Lightning relay (GPIO)
lightningGuard.pin.updateBridge: Update Rig Bridge: this bridge (version {{version}}) does not have the multi-display relay rules — it follows only the most recent display, does not hold the relay itself when a display goes quiet, and its headless guard does not pick up your guard settings. Download the current Rig Bridge from this tab, or run the updater.
lightningGuard.pin.wiring: A Pi pin gives 3.3 V and a few mA: drive a relay MODULE (transistor + flyback diode on board), never a bare coil. Use a relay or coax switch rated for your RF power, and disconnect only on receive. This is a convenience, not lightning protection — it does not replace grounding, bonding and surge arrestors.
lightningGuard.settings.channelPush: Web Push (also with the browser closed)
lightningGuard.settings.description: Watches real-time lightning (Blitzortung.org) around your station — also while the Lightning map layer is off. A strike inside the warning radius raises a warning, one inside the alarm radius an alarm; the all-clear comes after the set time without strikes nearby. Optional: a Rig Bridge relay disconnects the antenna during the alarm. (This replaces the former Lightning Proximity tone.)
lightningGuard.settings.hysteresisNote: A level starts at its radius but is held by strikes out to {{warnExit}} km (warning) and {{alarmExit}} km (alarm), so a storm on the edge does not flap the alarm. 0 % turns this off. Defaults: {{defaultWarn}} km warning, {{defaultAlarm}} km alarm, {{defaultPct}} %.
lightningGuard.settings.noLocation: Set your station location (Settings → Station) — distances are measured from DE.
lightningGuard.settings.notifyNeedsPermi: Turn on Browser Notifications at the top of this tab to allow notifications.
lightningGuard.settings.pushBroadcast: This server sends lightning pushes to every subscriber (PUSH_LIGHTNING_BROADCAST) — meant for a server only you use.
lightningGuard.settings.pushNote: Your station location (rounded to about 1 km) and radii are stored with this browser's push subscription on this server, so it can push strikes near you — also ones reported by other stations nearby. Untick to remove them.
lightningGuard.settings.pushSubscribeFai: Could not subscribe this browser to push ({{reason}}).
lightningGuard.settings.pushUnavailable: Web Push is not available here — it needs HTTPS and a server with Web Push keys (self-hosters: see the manual).
lightningGuard.settings.relayEnable: Drive the Rig Bridge lightning relay (GPIO lightningOut)
lightningGuard.settings.relayHowTo: Needs Rig Bridge enabled (local or Cloud Relay) with the GPIO plugin running and a relay line assigned in Settings → Rig Bridge. The relay releases automatically at the all-clear; if this browser goes away, Rig Bridge holds it for the all-clear time. With several displays it stays engaged while any of them wants it. The header ⚡ menu has a manual override.
lightningGuard.settings.repeatCloser: Alert again during an alarm when lightning comes much closer (half the distance, or inside 10 km; at most every 2 min)
lightningGuard.settings.safetyText: The guard is a convenience. Lightning data can be late, incomplete or missing, and the browser or network can fail. It does not replace proper grounding, bonding, surge arrestors and disconnecting by hand when a storm is coming.
lightningGuard.settings.testNote: A simulated strike runs the whole chain — alerts, banner, EmComm log, the relay and a test push to this browser only — and shows on the Lightning map layer. With "Strikes needed" above 1, click more than once.
lightningGuard.settings.title: Lightning guard

offlinePacks.custom.intro: For your own tile server (for example an mbtiles server on the shack Pi or the LAN) or a provider whose terms allow offline storage. It is added to the basemap list and offered for offline areas. You are responsible for following the source’s terms. The server must send CORS headers, and a plain-http server only works when OpenHamClock itself is opened over http on localhost.

Add OpenHamClock to the Home Screen (iOS) or Dock (macOS) and open it from there to keep them; check your areas before relying on them.

propVerify.help.beacons: Beacons: with the Rig Bridge KiwiSDR beacon monitor running, the best measured SNR of NCDXF beacons within {{km}} km of DX in the last 20 minutes — a real receiver on the far end of the path.
propVerify.help.observed: Spots: DX cluster and PSKReporter reports from the last 15 minutes whose two ends are on your continent and the DX continent. This measures who is on the air, not path quality — a quiet band on a weekday morning is not a wrong model.
propVerify.help.predicted: Predicted: ITU-R P.533 circuit reliability from your station to the DX target for this UTC hour, with your mode, power and antenna — the percentage of days the band supports the path at this hour. Recomputed when you change DX.

propVerify.help.status: Status: OPEN · confirmed = model ≥ 50 % and activity seen; OPEN · no spots yet = model open, nothing heard; MARGINAL = model 15–50 %; CLOSED = model < 15 % and nothing heard; OPEN · model said closed = model < 15 % but {{n}}+ spots on the path, so trust the air over the model.
propVerify.loadingPath: Running the P.533 prediction for this path…

station.settings.beaconMonitor.etiquette: The monitor holds one receiver slot 24/7. Prefer a Kiwi you own or have permission to park on; public receivers often cap session length per IP, and the monitor then reconnects with backoff.
station.settings.beaconMonitor.intro: Log NCDXF/IBP beacon SNR around the clock through a KiwiSDR. Rig Bridge does the listening (one receiver slot, retuned every 10-second beacon slot); results appear in the IBP Beacons panel's MEASURED view and in the Prediction Check panel.
station.settings.beaconMonitor.needsBrid: Enable Rig Bridge above first — the monitor runs inside it.

station.settings.beaconMonitor.pushOk: Rig Bridge updated — the monitor restarts with these settings
station.settings.beaconMonitor.title: Beacon monitor (KiwiSDR)
station.settings.bearings.hint: Magnetic bearings are corrected by the World Magnetic Model (WMM2025) declination at your station and shown with an "M" suffix — handy when aiming a beam with a compass or a rotator calibrated to magnetic north.
station.settings.bearings.title: Bearings
station.settings.brightness.auto: Auto brightness (light sensor via Rig Bridge)
station.settings.brightness.describe: Dims the display. With the Rig Bridge brightness plugin and a controllable backlight the panel itself dims and the display schedule switches it off; otherwise a dark overlay is used. Calibrate the light sensor on the Rig Bridge setup page.
station.settings.brightness.noBridge: Rig Bridge brightness plugin not detected — overlay dimming only.
station.settings.brightness.title: Brightness
station.settings.callbook.describe: Online callbook opened when you click a callsign in the UI.
station.settings.callbook.title: Callsign Lookup
station.settings.carto.describe: The Dark and Streets styles use Esri tiles by default. Paste a free CARTO key (carto.com/basemaps/apikey, 5M tiles/month) to switch them back to the original CARTO look with localized labels. The key is saved only in this browser — it is never synced to the server or shared with other users of this instance.
station.settings.carto.title: CARTO Basemap Key
station.settings.demo.describe: Makes a random harmless change every 30 seconds — a panel, a map layer, a DX picked from recent spots, or the basemap. Not saved: a reload turns it off.
station.settings.demo.title: Demo mode
station.settings.describe: Enter your callsign and grid square to get started. Settings are saved in your browser.
station.settings.dx.custom.callsign: Your callsign ({{callsign}}) will be used for login.
station.settings.dx.custom.title: 📡 Custom Telnet Server
station.settings.dx.custom.warning: ⚠️ Custom telnet requires self-hosted deployment (Pi/local). Cloud hosting (Railway/openhamclock.app) blocks outbound telnet.
station.settings.dx.describe: → Real-time DX Spider feed via our dedicated proxy service
station.settings.dx.hostedLockedDescribe: The hosted site uses our own cluster node — aggregating RBN, HamQTH, POTA, SOTA, WWFF, Parks n Peaks, DX Summit + user spots. Run your own OpenHamClock to connect to a custom cluster with your callsign.
station.settings.dx.loginCommands.help: Native cluster commands sent once after login, in order (e.g. set/filter dxbm/pass 20,15 or set/skimmer). One line each, max {{max}} commands, {{len}} characters; toggle a command off to keep it without sending it. Telnet clusters only — HTTP sources ignore these.
station.settings.dx.loginCommands.title: Cluster login commands
station.settings.dx.telnetOnlyNote: Cluster login commands and the Cluster Console panel are available only with a Custom Telnet Server source — HTTP and UDP sources have no session to talk to.
station.settings.dx.title: DX Cluster Source
station.settings.dx.udp.setDxHelp: Each new spot received over UDP (N1MM, DXLog, MacLoggerDX…) becomes the DX target, like HamClock.
station.settings.gps.clockWarning: GPS time differs from this computer's clock by {{secs}} s — check the system clock (warning only, nothing is changed).
station.settings.gps.describe: Use a GPS receiver attached to Rig Bridge for the station location. Enable the GPS plugin on the Rig Bridge setup page first. Set once applies the first fix after start-up; Follow keeps DE, the grid and logged QSOs on the live position (rover mode) and enables the Rover panel alerts.
station.settings.gps.status.noData: No GPS data from Rig Bridge
station.settings.gps.status.noFix: GPS connected — waiting for a fix
station.settings.gps.status.stale: GPS data stale — receiver stopped sending
station.settings.gps.title: GPS (Rig Bridge)
station.settings.grayscale.describe: Desaturate the map or the whole display — for monochrome screens, projectors and low-distraction shack displays.
station.settings.grayscale.title: Grayscale display
station.settings.idleClock.describe: Shows the big Clock layout when nobody has touched the screen for a while, and comes straight back to the previous layout on any touch, mouse or key. Turning this on turns Scene Rotation off, and vice versa.
station.settings.idleClock.title: Idle Clock
station.settings.kiosk.describe: A 4–8 digit PIN for touch displays in public places. While locked, Settings, layout changes and the command palette ask for the PIN; the padlock in the header locks and unlocks. Kiosk launch scripts can add ?lock=1 to the URL to start locked.
station.settings.kiosk.title: Kiosk lock
station.settings.layers.autoSpaceWx.desc: Turn the Aurora layer on when NOAA's aurora probability peaks above 50 % and the D-RAP layer on when absorption reaches 25 MHz; off again below 25 % / 15 MHz. Layers you toggle yourself are left alone for the session.
station.settings.layers.boundaryShowStat: Show US state and Canadian province lines
station.settings.layers.spotLabels.help: What the labels on DX cluster and activation (POTA/SOTA/WWFF/WWBOTA) markers show, and a minimum distance from DE below which labels are hidden so nearby spots do not clutter the map.
station.settings.layers.spotLabels.title: Spot labels
station.settings.layers.title: Map Layers
station.settings.layout.activator.descri: → In the field: self-spotting, activations, RBN checks, nearby repeaters — park/summit overlays on
station.settings.layout.airtraffic.descr: → Live aircraft and ATC sectors over a big map
station.settings.layout.clock.describe: → A big digital clock and nothing else — UTC and local, date, callsign. For shack TVs during down time
station.settings.layout.compact.describe: → Data-first layout for 4:3 and smaller screens
station.settings.layout.contest.describe: → Contest operating: quick-log strip with dupe check, rate meter, and session multipliers
station.settings.layout.eme.describe: → Moonbounce: 3D globe framed on Earth and Moon with the DE→Moon→DX legs, moon az/el at both ends, mutual windows, sky tracks, and EME cluster spots
station.settings.layout.hunter.describe: → Chasing activators: cluster, all activation programs, greyline — spot overlays and DX paths on
station.settings.layout.mobile.describe: → A phone or tablet as the main display: compact header, a touch-sized map, and swipeable panel cards. For go-boxes and the field
station.settings.layout.weather.describe: → Radar, lightning, hazards, and aurora on the map with weather panels
station.settings.licenseClass.hint: US license class shades out-of-privilege ranges on the band plan bar and warns (without blocking) when click-to-tune lands outside your privileges. Non-US? Leave it on Other — no restrictions are shown.
station.settings.licenseClass.title: License Class (US)
station.settings.logsync.describe: Push QSOs you log in OpenHamClock to Wavelog/Cloudlog or your QRZ Logbook, and pull LoTW confirmations into your local log. All credentials are stored only in this browser — never on the server, never in backups — and each request carries your own keys, so this works per-user on shared/hosted instances.
station.settings.logsync.lotw.describe: Pulls confirmed QSLs from Logbook of The World and marks matching QSOs in your local log (call + band + mode + time within 30 minutes). Uses your LoTW website login. LoTW is slow — syncs are limited to once every 5 minutes.
station.settings.logsync.lotw.title: LoTW confirmations
station.settings.logsync.qrz.describe: Uses a QRZ Logbook API key (Logbook → Settings → API on qrz.com; requires an XML subscription). This is NOT your QRZ username/password used for callsign lookups.
station.settings.logsync.qrz.title: QRZ Logbook push
station.settings.logsync.title: Logbook Sync
station.settings.logsync.wavelog.describ: New QSOs are pushed automatically (with a retry queue). The Station Profile ID is shown by the Test button, or in the URL when editing a station profile in Wavelog.
station.settings.logsync.wavelog.title: Wavelog / Cloudlog push
station.settings.monoFont.describe: Used in data displays — spot lists, callsigns, frequencies. Pick a slashed-zero variant to clearly distinguish 0 from 8.
station.settings.operatingMode.title: Propagation Mode & Power
station.settings.preventSleep.describe.o: Normal sleep behavior — display may dim or lock when idle.

station.settings.remote.describe: Lets a phone, a script or another computer drive this display through the /api/control API — set DE/DX, switch layout and theme, toggle layers, pick a satellite, shift time, tune the rig. Off by default on the hosted site.
station.settings.remote.enable: Allow remote control of this display
station.settings.remote.newIdHint: Replaces the display id and the pairing key — QR codes scanned before stop working.
station.settings.remote.pairingHint: The link and QR code carry this display's pairing key: anyone holding it can drive this display (and only this one). Treat it like a password.
station.settings.remote.pairingHintKeyed: This server also has an admin key (API_WRITE_KEY); your phone never needs it — the pairing key is enough.
station.settings.remote.qrHint: Scan with a phone on the same network to open the touch remote for this display.
station.settings.remote.rejectedHint: The server has this display id paired with another browser. Press New id to pair again.

station.settings.rigBridge.readme.headin: Read the README before setting up
station.settings.rigBridge.relayUnsigned: This browser has no relay command key, so Rig Bridge will refuse its PTT and transmit commands (and tuning after 31 January 2027). Disconnect and connect the Cloud Relay again, then paste the new settings into Rig Bridge.
station.settings.rigControl.apiToken.hin: Required when rig-bridge has authentication enabled (new installs). Find it at http://localhost:5555.
station.settings.rigControl.apiToken.pla: Paste token from rig-bridge setup UI

station.settings.timezone.describe: Set this if your local time shows incorrectly (e.g. same as UTC). Privacy browsers like Librewolf may spoof your timezone.

station.settings.titles.describe: Up to six titles separated by ; take turns in the callsign box every 10 seconds. Leave empty to show the callsign.
station.settings.titles.error.tooLong: Each title may be at most 60 characters

station.settings.watchlists.help: Three independent lists: DX cluster spots, activation spots (POTA/SOTA/WWFF/WWBOTA) and logbook rows. Red highlights matches, Only shows just matches, Not hides them. The same lists are editable from each panel’s filter dialog.
station.settings.watchlists.title: Watch lists
timeShift.hint: Shifts the terminator, gray line, sun & moon, satellites and VOACAP hour. Live spots are not shifted. Keys: [ ] ±1 h, { } ±1 day, 0 = now.
timeShift.title: Time Shift
tropical.dxLocked: DX is locked — click to expand
tropical.title: TROPICAL CYCLONES
watchlist.help: Comma-separated specs; a spot matches when every part of any one spec fits. Parts: bands (40M, 20-10M), sub-bands (40CW, 20SSB, 30FT8, 160-10CW; modes CW DATA FT4 FT8 RTTY SSB), frequencies in MHz (14-14.02MHZ), logbook keywords NADXCC NAPREF NAGRID NABAND (not yet worked), and prefixes (VP2E matches VP2E/K0CJH and K0CJH/VP2E; a trailing / matches the DX portion only).
weather.error.rateLimitedTooltip: Get a free API key at open-meteo.com, then in your browser console (F12) run: localStorage.setItem('ohc_openmeteo_apikey', 'YOUR_KEY')

winlinkReach.aboveMufTitle: Above the predicted MUF ({{muf}} MHz, a monthly median): the band supports this frequency on half the days or fewer, so it is never rated Good.
winlinkReach.engine.wasm: ITU-R P.533, computed in your browser
winlinkReach.floorTitle: {{mode}} holds a link down to {{floor}} dB SNR (3 kHz) — {{source}}
winlinkReach.footnote2: Reliability is the share of days this hour the path can hold a link in the gateway’s mode (monthly median model). Good ≥ {{good}}%; Marginal ≥ {{marginal}}% or SNR margin ≥ {{margin}} dB; Off the air = outside the gateway’s published hours. ≈ marks a band-level estimate for a 60 m or out-of-band channel. VHF/UHF is by distance only. Click a gateway to set it as DX; with rig control connected it also tunes the dial frequency.
winlinkReach.hoursUnknownPerDay: Published hours "{{text}}": about {{n}} h a day, but not which hours — it may be off the air now.
winlinkReach.hoursUnknownShort: Hours unknown ("{{text}}") — may be off the air now
winlinkReach.hoursUnknownTitle: Published hours "{{text}}" do not say when it is on the air — it may be off the air now.
